genius.notes: Retain the October 1, 2026 scoped withdrawal of the former categorical non-payment exclusion. ONyc is documented as a transferable fractional segregated-account reinsurance exposure with variable NAV and conditional USDG liquidity quotes. Its issuer description alone does not establish a qualified U.S. securities exclusion or conclusively resolve all token governing obligations under section 2(22). On Re SAC Ltd. is identified in platform terms and independently named by the BMA as a graduated Class IIGB insurer also licensed under the Digital Asset Business Act. Those Bermuda licenses are separate from GENIUS approval or an OCC registered foreign exception. Current dated public-record checks resolve authorization unknown to no-public-authorization-found, without resolving applicability or asserting wrongdoing. DASP not-yet-restricted reflects the pre-effective federal regime and future offer/sale restriction, not an exemption or independent U.S. distribution permission. Apex monthly NAV attestations listed in issuer documentation concern investment valuation; no GENIUS monthly reserve assurance is asserted. Independent verification used issuer markdown/PDF sources and isolated Chromium for the OCC pending-bank-application and BMA tables. Indexed enforcement searches located no matching SEC, OCC, NYDFS or FDIC action; these limited searches do not establish the absence of private or non-public proceedings.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: On 2026-10-07, no public GENIUS issuer approval, state qualification, official pending application or registered foreign exception naming On Re SAC Ltd. for ONyc was found in the inspected directories, rulemaking materials, issuer disclosures and targeted regulator-domain searches. The OCC table concerns pending bank licensing, and NYDFS listings concern existing state licenses; neither is a complete GENIUS approval census. Rulemaking is pre-effective; absence does not establish illegality, refusal or absence of non-public applications. Token applicability remains independently unresolved.
